feat(docs): /playground is the card at full width (rich-example-card-obsb.cau) (#356)

* feat(docs): /playground is the card at full width (rich-example-card-obsb.cau)

The playground is the example card: line numbers on, setup unfolded, the
edited line always shown, the program in the hash. Try it carries the card's
program, setup groups included (card.<deflated JSON>); a hash in the old
format opens as a program with no setup.

The card decides how to show a playground program from what it does: a
static run is drawn; one that redraws, listens on stdin, leaves a timer
running past its body, or is still running at the limit moves to the live
terminal. RichPlayground.ts is deleted.

* fix(docs): one rule for what only a terminal shows, in the build and the browser (rich-example-card-obsb.cau)

Review (high) of #356:
- scanEscapes (example-fragments.ts) is the one reading of which escapes a
  drawing drops; the build's disallowedEscape and the browser's CSI-only
  redraws are gone. ESC 7/8, ESC M, ESC c and non-link OSC now end a static
  run; erase in line, which decodeAnsi draws, passes the build too.
- Timers are bound lexically by runInTerminal and counted there; runsOn is
  the one 'runs on' rule. The worker no longer patches its global timers, and
  the build refuses a static block whose card program leaves a timer set.
- A card link's setup lines may hold no line break and its code no \r; the
  slicer now emits a multi-line carried statement as one Line per line.
- Mod-Enter runs the edit at once instead of after the typing debounce.
- e2e no-break-space helpers use an explicit \u00a0; the redraw test now
  exercises the escape path, with the timer path its own test.
- Dead .rich-live-button:disabled and duplicate .rich-playground colour
  selectors removed; MAX_PROGRAM_BYTES says it bounds the packed JSON, and a
  test pins that boundary.

* fix(docs): the build and the static run agree on stdin, unfinished escapes and timer order (rich-example-card-obsb.cau)

Review (medium) of #356:
- The build refuses a static block whose card program listens on stdin, as
  the page's static run ends one.
- undrawnEscape moves to example-fragments.ts; the static run applies it to
  what is left unread when a program ends, as the build does.
- scanEscapes drops an escape as soon as it can no longer become one a
  drawing draws, and bounds an open link at 4096 chars, so the per-write
  re-read is bounded.
- Program timer delays are taken as Node takes them (under 1 ms is 1 ms) and
  runsOn waits 1 ms, so it answers alike in Node and a browser.
